Inventory Allocation Notes

Inventory should be allocated according to sell-through velocity, strategic boutique priority, and launch calendar.
The first allocation wave should favor stores with proven conversion on high-margin references.
Secondary reallocation between regions is allowed when stock cover exceeds eight weeks in a low-demand location and falls below three weeks in a priority market.

For limited editions, allocation must remain centrally controlled.
For iconic permanent collectio
n items, local commercial teams may propose reallocations supported by weekly sales evidence.

Monthly Operations Report – June

The main operational risks identified this month were:
- delayed inbound shipments for high-demand references,
- stock imbalance between Western Europe and the Swiss market,
- temporary shortage of leather packaging components,
- higher return handling time in two flagship stores.

No critical IT outage was reported.
The operations team recommends tighter weekly stock reallocation reviews and earlier supplier confirmation for packaging materials.

Pricing Policy – Europe Luxury Retail

Standard discounting is not permitted for core collection products.
Any exception request must be approved by the regional commercial director and justified by one of the following conditions:
1. end-of-season stock clearance,
2. damaged packaging with intact product quality,
3. VIP retention case with documented revenue history,
4. local event-driven traffic activation approved in advance.

Discount exceptions above 10% require finance review.
Repeated dis

counting in the same boutique within a 60-day period must be escalated.
The objective is to protect brand equity while allowing controlled flexibility in exceptional cases.
